langCode.description: This translation's language code (en, de, pt_BR…), used as the page's lang attribute.

extDescription.message: Weighs your search results: tag, rerank, and hide sites, with lists anyone can publish.
extDescription.description: Shown in the stores and the browser's add-ons page. At most 132 characters.

commandToggleEnabled.description: Keyboard shortcut, listed in the browser's shortcut settings.

commandToggleHidden.message: Show hidden results, or hide them again
commandToggleHidden.description: Keyboard shortcut, listed in the browser's shortcut settings.

levelHide.description: A site's ranking. The five rankings are Hide, Lower, Normal, Raise, and Pin.

levelPin.description: A site's ranking: always at the top.

popupOn.description: In the toolbar popup. Under the on/off switch while Anubis is on.

popupOff.message: Off. Search pages are left as they are.
popupOff.description: In the toolbar popup. Under the on/off switch while Anubis is off.

popupOnLabel.description: Screen reader label of the on/off switch.

popupAddSite.description: In the toolbar popup. A button and heading for adding a site by hand. Also in Settings → Your sites.

popupRanking.description: Screen reader label of the ranking menu next to Add a site.

popupNoSites.message: Nothing yet. Use the ⚖ button on any search result to rank its site.
popupNoSites.description: In the toolbar popup. Under “Your sites” (popupYourSites) while you’ve ranked none.

popupKeptNormal.description: A site set to Normal on purpose, overriding lists.

popupListsAndTags.description: $1 is the number of lists (popupListCount), $2 the number of tags (popupTagCount).

popupListCount_one.description: In the toolbar popup. At the foot: how many lists you subscribe to. Also in Settings.

popupTagCount_one.description: How many tags there are, in the toolbar popup and Settings.

popupRankingFor.description: Screen reader label; $1 is a site.

popupRankPin.message: Pin $1 to the top of search results

popupYourSites.description: Heading over the last few sites in your list, in the toolbar popup.

popupSeeAll.description: Opens Settings → Your sites. $1 is how many sites you've ranked.

popupOpenLists.description: In the toolbar popup. Tooltip of the list and tag count at the foot.

popupShowOnly.description: Heading over the tags on this page's results; choosing one shows only its results.

popupTags.description: Heading over a site’s tags, in the toolbar popup; also the Tags column in Settings → Your sites.

popupSite.description: Screen reader label of the menu that picks how much of a site a ranking covers.

popupSiteChoice.message: Choose how much of the site this applies to
popupSiteChoice.description: In the toolbar popup. Tooltip of the menu that picks how much of a site (fandom.com or harrypotter.fandom.com) a ranking applies to.

popupHintAllow.description: In the toolbar popup. Under the rankings, for a site you set to Normal on purpose.

popupHintMine.message: Your choice for $1, on every search.

popupHintLists.message: $1 by $2. Choose one to decide yourself.
popupHintLists.description: $1 is a ranking in the past tense (Hidden, Raised…), $2 the lists that chose it.

popupHintNone.message: Your choice applies on every search.
popupHintNone.description: In the toolbar popup. Under the rankings, for a site you haven’t ranked.

popupYourTagSettings.description: Stands in for a list's name in popupHintLists when a tag you chose to hide or raise decided the ranking.

popupTagFrom.description: $1 is the lists that tag this site.

popupTagSite.description: $1 is a site, $2 a tag's name.

popupTagInvalid.message: Enter a tag name with at least one letter or number.
popupTagInvalid.description: Shown under the new-tag field when its name cannot be used.

popupTagAlreadySet.message: That tag is already on this site.
popupTagAlreadySet.description: Shown when someone tries to add a tag that is already on the current site.

tagSiteReason.message: Why this site fits the “$1” tag (optional)
tagSiteReason.description: Label for an optional explanation when someone adds a site to a tag in Settings.

popupThisPage.description: In the toolbar popup. Heading over what Anubis did on this page, when the engine isn’t known.

popupThisPageOn.description: $1 is a search engine, e.g. Google.

popupNotSearch.message: Search on Google, DuckDuckGo, Bing, Brave, or another supported engine to see what Anubis changes.
popupNotSearch.description: In the toolbar popup. On a page that isn’t a search page.

showHidden.description: Button in the summary above the results and in the toolbar popup: brings back the results Anubis hid on this page.

hideAgain.description: Hides the results Show hidden brought back.

loadMore.description: Button in the summary above the results and in the toolbar popup: adds the next page of results to this one.

loadMoreTitle.message: Add the next page of results to this page and rank them together

loading.description: loadMore while the next page loads.

loadMoreEmpty.message: $1 sent no results for page $2. It may want you to confirm you’re not a robot first.
loadMoreEmpty.description: In the summary above the results, when Load more results got a page without results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreRepeat.message: $1 sent the same results again for page $2, so there are no more.
loadMoreRepeat.description: In the summary above the results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreBusy.message: $1 asked Anubis to slow down before page $2. Try again in a minute.
loadMoreBusy.description: In the summary above the results, when the engine answered “too many requests”. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreRefused.description: In the summary above the results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreSlow.message: $1 took too long to send page $2.
loadMoreSlow.description: In the summary above the results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreFailed.description: In the summary above the results, when the request failed. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreOpen.description: Link after loadMoreEmpty and the like: opens the page Anubis tried to load in a new tab. $1 is the page number.

loadMoreOpenTitle.message: Open it in a new tab to see what $1 sent
loadMoreOpenTitle.description: Tooltip of loadMoreOpen. $1 is the search engine.

chipFromPage.description: Under a result's title when Load more results brought it in. $1 is the page number.

barHidden.description: In the line standing for a hidden result, after the site: “fandom.com hidden”.

barHiddenByYou.description: In the line standing for a hidden result, after the site.

barHiddenByTag.description: In the line standing for a hidden result, after the site. $1 is a tag's name.

barHiddenByLens.description: In the line standing for a hidden result, after the site. $1 is a list that only includes sites it names.

barHiddenByList.description: In the line standing for a hidden result, after the site. $1 is a list's name.

menuWhyHeading.description: Heading in the menu on a result, over the lists' reasons for its ranking.

menuNewTagPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the field in the menu on a result where you name a new tag.

menuNewTagLabel.description: Screen reader label of menuNewTagPlaceholder's field.

menuAddTagButton.description: Button after the new tag field in the menu on a result.

menuSavedNote.description: At the foot of the menu on a result, once you've ranked or tagged its site.

menuCloseLabel.description: Label and tooltip of the × that closes the menu on a result.

anubisSettings.description: Label of the cog button that opens settings, in the toolbar popup, the summary above the results, and the menu on each result.

help.description: In the toolbar popup. Link at the foot to the wiki.

reportProblem.description: Link in the toolbar popup and the settings sidebar that opens a bug report on GitHub.

reportProblemTitle.message: Open a bug report on GitHub, with Anubis’s version and your browser filled in

summaryShowAll.description: In the summary above the results, while only results with one tag are shown.

summaryFilterLabel.description: Screen reader label of the row of tags in the summary above the results.

summaryFilterOn.description: Tooltip of a tag in the summary above the results. $1 is the tag's name.

summaryFilterOff.description: Tooltip of the tag whose results are the only ones shown.

summaryPinned.description: One part of summaryActed: $1 results were pinned. The parts are joined into a list (“pinned 1, raised 2, and hid 2”).

summaryRaised.description: Like summaryPinned, for results that were raised.

summaryLowered.description: Like summaryPinned, for results that were lowered.

summaryHid.description: Like summaryPinned, for results that were hidden.

summaryActed.description: The summary above the results. $1 is the list of summaryPinned, summaryRaised… parts, $2 is summaryResults or summaryResultsPages, e.g. “Anubis raised 1 and hid 2 of 7 results.”

summaryResults_one.description: How many results the page has, for summaryActed.

summaryResultsPages_one.description: Like summaryResults, after Load more results brought in more pages. $2 is the number of pages, always 2 or more.

summaryAlsoRemoved.description: Second sentence of the summary, after summaryActed, when clean-up removed blocks from the page. $1 is the list of summaryRemoved… parts, e.g. “an AI answer and 2 video panels”.

summaryRemovedOnly.description: The summary when clean-up removed blocks but no result was ranked. $1 is as in summaryAlsoRemoved.

summaryShortActed.description: The summary on phones, where the full sentence (summaryActed) takes several lines; Details shows it. $1 is how many results were pinned, raised, lowered, or hidden, $2 is summaryResults or summaryResultsPages, e.g. “Anubis changed 4 of 9 results.”

summaryShortActedRemoved.message: Anubis changed $1 of $2 and cleaned up the page.
summaryShortActedRemoved.description: Like summaryShortActed, when clean-up also removed blocks from the page.

summaryShortRemoved.description: The summary on phones when clean-up removed blocks but no result was ranked; Details shows summaryRemovedOnly.

summaryDetails.description: Button in the summary on phones: shows the full summary, the page's tags, Load more results, and settings.

summaryFewerDetails.description: Button in the summary on phones: folds away what summaryDetails showed.

summaryUnchanged_one.message: Anubis left this result as it was.
summaryUnchanged_one.description: The summary when Anubis changed nothing on a page with one result.

summaryUnchanged_other.message: Anubis left all $1 results as they were.
summaryUnchanged_other.description: The summary when Anubis changed nothing. $1 is the number of results.

summaryUnchangedPages.message: Anubis left all $1 results from $2 pages as they were.
summaryUnchangedPages.description: Like summaryUnchanged, after Load more results brought in more pages. $2 is the number of pages.

summaryFiltered_one.description: The summary while only results with one tag are shown. $1 is the number of results on the page, $2 the tag's name, $3 how many results have it.

summaryRemovedAi_one.description: A part of summaryAlsoRemoved: blocks clean-up removed. $1 is how many.

summaryRemovedDiscussions_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for panels of forum threads.

summaryRemovedNews_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for news panels (“Top stories”).

summaryRemovedImages_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for rows of images.

summaryRemovedRelated_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for lists of related searches.

summaryRemovedElsewhere_one.message: a row of other search engines
summaryRemovedElsewhere_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for rows of buttons that repeat the search on other engines.

withShortcut.description: A button's description followed by its keyboard shortcut, e.g. Show hidden (Alt+Shift+H).

toolbarOff.description: Tooltip of the toolbar button while Anubis is turned off.

weighLabel.description: Tooltip and screen reader label of the balance button on each result, and the name of the menu it opens. $1 is the result's site, e.g. fandom.com.

weighLabelRanked.description: The same label for a site that isn't ranked Normal, whose button shows its ranking. Keep it starting with weighLabel's words. $1 is the site; $2 is chipHidden, chipLowered, chipRaised, or chipPinned in lower case, e.g. “Hide, rank, or tag fandom.com (lowered)”.

hiddenShow.description: Button on the line standing for a hidden result: shows that result.

hiddenShowSite.description: Screen reader label of hiddenShow, naming the site. Keep it starting with hiddenShow's word. $1 is the site, e.g. fandom.com.

hiddenMore_one.description: After a site's name on the one line standing for several hidden results in a row, e.g. “fandom.com and 1 more hidden by your list”.

summaryChangedHide.description: In the summary above the results, after you rank a site from the menu on a result, followed by an Undo button. $1 is the site, e.g. fandom.com.

summaryChangedAllow.description: Like summaryChangedHide, for Normal when a subscribed list ranks the site: it's then ranked Normal whatever the lists say. Normal is the ranking's name, as on the menu's button.

summaryChangedNormal.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after you press the ranking a site already had, so your list no longer ranks it and the subscribed lists decide.

summaryChangedTagOn.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after you tag a site. $1 is the site, $2 the tag's name.

summaryChangedTagOff.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after you untag a site. $1 is the site, $2 the tag's name.

summaryChangedSite.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after several changes to one site's ranking and tags.

summaryUndo.description: Button after summaryChangedHide and the like: puts the site back as it was before. Also after deleting something in Settings: brings it back.

menuSuggest.message: Should a list include it? Suggest it to $1.
menuSuggest.description: In the menu on a result, once you've ranked or tagged the site yourself. $1 is one or two list names, each a link that opens a pre-filled issue on that list's issue tracker, joined like “A or B”.

menuSuggestTitle.message: Propose $1 to $2 on its issue tracker
menuSuggestTitle.description: Tooltip of a list's name in menuSuggest. $1 is a site, $2 the list's name.

menuReport.description: In the menu on a result, under the lines saying what each list does with it. $1 is those lists' names, each a link that opens a pre-filled issue on that list's issue tracker, joined like “A or B”.

menuMatchedRule.description: Shown below a list's explanation in the result menu, above the exact rule from the list. $1 is a line number.

menuReportTitle.message: Tell $1 it’s wrong about this result, on its issue tracker
menuReportTitle.description: Tooltip of a list's name in menuReport. $1 is the list's name.

offerTitle.description: Settings → Lists, after a subscribe link opened it. $1 is the list's name.

offerTrust.message: A list can hide, rank, and tag sites in your results. Only subscribe to lists you trust.
offerTrust.description: Settings → Lists, under offerTitle, for a list that isn’t in Anubis’s directory.

offerPermission.message: Your browser will then ask to let Anubis read from $1, the site the list is on.

offerSubscribe.description: Settings → Lists: the button that subscribes to a list.

offerCancel.description: A button that closes a form without saving, in Settings.

welcomeTitle.description: Tab title of the page that opens when Anubis is installed.

welcomeHeading.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Its heading.

welcomeIntro.message: It tags, reranks, and hides search results, following your own choices and the lists you subscribe to.
welcomeIntro.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Under the heading.

welcomePinHeading.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Heading of the step about the toolbar button.

welcomePinWhy.message: Its toolbar button shows what Anubis did on the page, turns it on or off, and ranks the site you're on.
welcomePinWhy.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Under welcomePinHeading.

welcomePinChrome.message: Press the Extensions button (the puzzle piece) next to the address bar, then the pin beside Anubis.
welcomePinChrome.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. How to keep Anubis’s button on the toolbar in this browser. Use the names the browser shows in your language. For Chrome.

welcomePinEdge.message: Press the Extensions button (the puzzle piece) next to the address bar, then the eye beside Anubis.
welcomePinEdge.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. How to keep Anubis’s button on the toolbar in this browser. Use the names the browser shows in your language. For Edge.

welcomePinOpera.message: Press the Extensions button (the cube) next to the address bar, then the pin beside Anubis.
welcomePinOpera.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. How to keep Anubis’s button on the toolbar in this browser. Use the names the browser shows in your language. For Opera.

welcomePinFirefox.message: Press the Extensions button (the puzzle piece) next to the address bar, then the gear beside Anubis, and choose Pin to Toolbar.
welcomePinFirefox.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. How to keep Anubis’s button on the toolbar in this browser. Use the names the browser shows in your language. For Firefox on a computer.

welcomePinAndroid.message: Anubis is in the browser's menu, under Extensions.
welcomePinAndroid.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. For Firefox for Android, which has no toolbar for extensions. Use the names Firefox shows in your language.

welcomePinned.description: Shown instead of the steps once the browser says the button is pinned.

welcomeSearchHeading.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Heading of the step about searching.

welcomeSearchHow.message: Search as you usually do. To hide, rank, or tag a site, point at one of its results and press the ⚖ button.
welcomeSearchHow.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Under welcomeSearchHeading.

welcomeSearchFor.message: Search for “$1” to see tags from your lists:
welcomeSearchFor.description: $1 is welcomeQuery. Followed by one link per search engine.

welcomeSearchOn.description: Tooltip of a search engine link. $1 is welcomeQuery, $2 a search engine, e.g. Google.

welcomeQuery.description: A search whose results include official documentation, forums, and Wikipedia, so the starter lists show their tags. Keep it technical.

welcomeListsHeading.description: Heading over the lists you subscribe to, on the welcome page and in Settings → Lists.

welcomeListsIntro.message: Lists tag, raise, lower, or hide sites for you. You start with these:
welcomeListsIntro.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Before the lists you start with.

welcomeListsNone.message: Lists tag, raise, lower, or hide sites for you. You aren't subscribed to any yet.
welcomeListsNone.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Instead of welcomeListsIntro, when you subscribe to no lists.

welcomeListsMore.message: Turn these off, or find more lists, in the settings.
welcomeListsMore.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. After the lists you start with.

welcomeListsOpen.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A button that opens Settings → Lists.

welcomeGuide.description: A link to the wiki, on the welcome page and in the settings sidebar.

welcomePrivacy.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A link to the privacy policy.

syncHeading.description: Settings → Sync: the section’s heading, also in the sidebar.

syncIntro.message: Your list and settings on your other computers, and in your other browsers.

syncBrowserHeading.description: Settings → Sync: heading over the browser’s own sync.

syncFirefox.message: Your list, settings, tag choices, and subscriptions are saved in Firefox's sync storage. Firefox copies them to your other computers when you're signed in to Firefox with Add-ons ticked in its sync settings. It syncs about every 10 minutes, or when you choose Sync Now.
syncFirefox.description: Settings → Sync: in Firefox on a computer. “Add-ons” and “Sync Now” are Firefox’s own names; use the ones Firefox shows in your language.

syncFirefoxAndroid.message: Firefox for Android doesn't sync add-on data, so your list, settings, tag choices, and subscriptions stay on this device. To sync them, connect a WebDAV server below.
syncFirefoxAndroid.description: Settings → Sync: in Firefox for Android.

syncChrome.message: Your list, settings, tag choices, and subscriptions are saved in the browser's sync storage. The browser copies them to your other computers when you're signed in to it with extensions syncing.
syncChrome.description: Settings → Sync: in Chrome, Edge, and other Chromium browsers.

syncBrowserHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

syncUsage.message: They take $1 KB of the $2 KB sync has room for.

syncTooBig.message: Your list is too big for sync, so it's saved on this device only. Your settings, tag choices, and subscriptions still sync.
syncTooBig.description: Settings → Sync: when your list doesn’t fit in the browser’s sync storage.

webdavHeading.description: Settings → Sync: heading over syncing through a WebDAV server.

webdavIntro.message: Firefox and Chrome don't natively sync with one another. To share between them, you can connect the same WebDAV storage in each. Koofr and InfiniCLOUD have free plans, and self-hosted options such as Nextcloud work as well. Anubis keeps one file there, anubis-sync.json, and combines the changes from each browser.
webdavIntro.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: under webdavHeading. Koofr, InfiniCLOUD, and Nextcloud are services; anubis-sync.json is a file name.

webdavHelp.message: Where to get an address and a password
webdavHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

webdavAddress.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: label of the server address field.

webdavAddressHint.message: The service's WebDAV address, starting with https://
webdavAddressHint.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: under webdavAddress.

listPermissionDenied.message: Anubis needs permission to read $1 to update this list.
listPermissionDenied.description: $1 is the list host name, e.g. example.org.

webdavUser.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: label of the user name field.

webdavPassword.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: label of the password field.

webdavPasswordHint.message: Most services give you a separate password for apps. Use that one.
webdavPasswordHint.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: under webdavPassword.

webdavConnect.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: the button that connects to the server.

webdavEncrypt.message: Encrypt the sync file end to end (recommended)
webdavEncrypt.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: a checkbox.

webdavEncryptionPassphrase.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: label of the passphrase field.

webdavConfirmPassphrase.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: label of the field that repeats the passphrase.

webdavEncryptionHint.message: Use a long, unique passphrase in every browser (at least 12 characters). It is saved in this browser only, never sent to the server. If you forget it, the server copy can't be recovered.
webdavEncryptionHint.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: under the passphrase fields.

webdavCorrectPassphrase.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: heading when the passphrase saved here can’t read the server’s file.

webdavCorrectPassphraseHint.message: Use the same passphrase you set in the other browser. It is saved here only and never sent to the server.
webdavCorrectPassphraseHint.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: under webdavCorrectPassphrase.

webdavSavePassphrase.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: a button.

webdavChangePassphrase.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: a button, and the heading of the form it opens.

webdavChangePassphraseHint.message: Anubis checks the current passphrase before changing the server file. Enter the new passphrase in every other browser before its next sync.
webdavChangePassphraseHint.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: under webdavChangePassphrase.

webdavChangePassphraseHelp.message: What happens when you change it
webdavChangePassphraseHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

webdavEncryptionShort.message: Use an encryption passphrase of at least 12 characters.
webdavEncryptionShort.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: when the passphrase is too short.

webdavPassphraseMismatch.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: when the two passphrase fields differ.

webdavEncrypted.message: The sync file is encrypted end to end. Its passphrase is saved in this browser only; the server cannot read the contents. Use the same passphrase in each browser. If you forget it, the server copy can't be recovered.
webdavEncrypted.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: while connected with encryption.

webdavEncryptionPending.message: Encryption is set up here. The next successful sync will encrypt the server copy. Use the same passphrase in each browser.
webdavEncryptionPending.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: after encryption is set up, before the next sync.

webdavEncryptionMissing.message: This browser has no encryption passphrase set. Use the same passphrase as the other browser to read an encrypted file. A plain sync file can be read by the server operator.
webdavEncryptionMissing.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: when the server’s file is encrypted and this browser has no passphrase.

webdavPrivacy.message: With encryption on, only encrypted data goes to this server; your passphrase is saved here and never sent. Without encryption, the server can read the sync file. Your WebDAV login is saved here and sent to this server to sign in.
webdavPrivacy.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: what is sent to the server.

webdavBadAddress.message: Enter the service's WebDAV address, starting with https://
webdavBadAddress.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: when the address isn’t an https:// address.

webdavMissingLogin.message: Enter the user name and password too.
webdavMissingLogin.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: when the user name or password is empty.

webdavDenied.message: Anubis needs your permission to send your list to $1.
webdavDenied.description: $1 is the server's host name, e.g. app.koofr.net.

webdavConnected.description: $1 is the server's host name, $2 the user name.

webdavWhen.message: Changes go to the server a few seconds after you make them. Changes from your other browsers come in when the browser starts and when you search, at most every 5 minutes.
webdavWhen.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: while connected: when changes are sent and fetched.

webdavSyncing.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: while a sync runs.

webdavLastSync.description: $1 is a time, or a date and time.

webdavLastTried.description: $1 is a time, or a date and time.

webdavSyncNow.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: a button.

webdavDisconnect.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: a button.

webdavDisconnected.message: Disconnected. The file stays on the server, and your list and settings stay here.
webdavDisconnected.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: after disconnecting.

webdavErrorAuth.message: The server didn't accept the user name or password. Many services need an app password here, not your usual one.
webdavErrorAuth.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: why syncing failed.

webdavErrorForbidden.message: The server doesn't let this account save files there.
webdavErrorForbidden.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: why syncing failed.

webdavErrorFolder.message: There's no folder at that address on the server. Check the address.
webdavErrorFolder.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: why syncing failed.

webdavErrorPermission.message: Anubis no longer has permission to sync with $1. Press Sync now to allow it again.

webdavErrorNetwork.message: Couldn't reach $1. Check the address and your connection.

webdavErrorFile.message: The anubis-sync.json file there isn't one Anubis can read, so it was left alone. Use another folder.
webdavErrorFile.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: why syncing failed. anubis-sync.json is a file name.

webdavErrorNeedsPassphrase.message: This sync file is encrypted. Enter its passphrase; nothing was changed.
webdavErrorNeedsPassphrase.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: why syncing failed.

webdavErrorWrongPassphrase.message: That passphrase couldn't decrypt the sync file. Check it; the server file was left unchanged.
webdavErrorWrongPassphrase.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: why syncing failed.

webdavErrorUnencrypted.message: This connection was encrypted before, but the server now has a plain-text sync file. It was left unchanged. Check the server file before syncing again.
webdavErrorUnencrypted.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: why syncing failed.

webdavErrorChanged.message: The sync file changed during the passphrase change, or the server cannot protect it from concurrent edits. Nothing was overwritten. Sync again and retry.
webdavErrorChanged.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: why syncing failed.

webdavErrorUnconfirmed.message: The connection to $1 dropped while it saved the file, so Anubis can't tell which passphrase it has now. The old passphrase is still saved here. If the next sync says it's wrong, enter the new one.

webdavErrorServer.message: The server answered with an error (HTTP $1). Try again later.
webdavErrorServer.description: $1 is an HTTP status code, e.g. 500.

webdavErrorFailed.description: Settings → Sync, Between browsers: why syncing failed.

appearanceHeading.description: Settings → Appearance: the section’s heading, also in the sidebar.

appearanceIntro.message: How Anubis looks here and on search pages.

themeHeading.description: Settings → Appearance: the light or dark setting. Also the screen reader label of its three buttons.

themeHint.message: Auto follows your browser here and in the menu on each result, and each search engine’s own light or dark mode for the rest of what Anubis adds to its pages.
themeHint.description: Settings → Appearance: explains themeHeading. “Auto” is themeAuto.

paletteHint.message: Plain draws everything Anubis adds to search pages in grey, with no gold. Tags lose their colours and are told apart by their names. Settings and the toolbar popup stay gold.
paletteHint.description: Settings → Appearance: explains paletteHeading. “Plain” is palettePlain.

paletteGold.description: Settings → Appearance: a choice for paletteHeading, the default.

palettePlain.description: Settings → Appearance: a choice for paletteHeading.

hideStyleHeading.description: Settings → Appearance: how hidden results look.

hideStyleHint.message: Remove takes them off the page; the summary above the results counts them, and Show hidden brings them back. Collapse leaves one slim line for each run of hidden results. Dim fades them.
hideStyleHint.description: Settings → Appearance: explains the three choices, hideStyleRemove, hideStyleCollapse, and hideStyleDim. “Show hidden” is showHidden.

hideStyleRemove.description: Settings → Appearance: a choice for hideStyleHeading.

hideStyleCollapse.description: Settings → Appearance: a choice for hideStyleHeading.

hideStyleDim.description: Settings → Appearance: a choice for hideStyleHeading.

rerankHint.message: Move raised and pinned results up and lowered ones down, like a Brave Goggle.
rerankHint.description: Settings → Appearance: explains rerankHeading. Brave Goggles are a product name.

rerankHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

deeperAuto.description: Settings → Appearance: a number of pages to add to each search.

deeperAutoHint.message: Add the next pages of results to the first one and rank them together, so a site you pinned on page 3 rises to the top. “Load more results” above the results does the same when you ask. Type how many pages to add, from 0 (off) to $1.
deeperAutoHint.description: Settings → Appearance: explains deeperAuto. $1 is the most pages allowed. “Load more results” is loadMore.

deeperHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

deeperUnit.description: After the number field of deeperAuto, like “2 more pages”.

deeperTipOff.message: Off: more results load only when you press “Load more results”.
deeperTipOff.description: Under deeperAuto when it is 0. “Load more results” is loadMore.

deeperTipTime_one.message: Adds about $1 second to each search.
deeperTipTime_one.description: Starts deeperTipFew, deeperTipSome, and deeperTipMany. $1 is a number of seconds.

deeperTipTime_other.message: Adds about $1 seconds to each search.

deeperTipFew.message: $1 Engines rarely mind a few pages.
deeperTipFew.description: Under deeperAuto for 1 to 3 pages. $1 is deeperTipTime.

deeperTipSome.message: $1 Some engines may start asking you to confirm you’re not a robot.
deeperTipSome.description: Under deeperAuto for 4 to 9 pages. $1 is deeperTipTime.

deeperTipMany.message: $1 Google and Bing often ask you to confirm you’re not a robot after this many. Some engines run out of pages before then.
deeperTipMany.description: Under deeperAuto for 10 pages. $1 is deeperTipTime.

chipsHeading.description: Settings → Appearance: a switch for the labels under results.

chipsHint.message: Show tags and rankings under each result title.

summaryHeading.description: Settings → Appearance: a switch for the line above the results.

summaryHint.message: Show a one-line summary of what Anubis changed above the results.

enabledHeading.description: Settings → Appearance: the switch that turns Anubis on or off.

enabledHint.message: Turn this off to leave search pages alone without uninstalling.

enginesHeading.description: Settings → Search engines: the section’s heading, also in the sidebar.

enginesIntro.message: Anubis works on web results from these engines. Results are found by page structure where possible, so small redesigns don’t break it.
enginesIntro.description: Settings → Search engines: under the heading.

enginesTrouble.message: Anubis doing nothing on a search page?
enginesTrouble.description: Settings → Search engines: followed by enginesTroubleHelp, a link.

enginesTroubleHelp.description: Link to the wiki’s troubleshooting page, after enginesTrouble.

shareHeading.description: Settings → Backup: the section’s heading. The sidebar says backupHeading.

shareIntro.message: Keep a copy of everything, bring your sites over from another tool, or publish your list for others to subscribe to.

publishIntro.message: No server needed: a public git repository is the database, and pull requests are how people contribute.

publishHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

publishStepDownload.message: Download your list below. Set its $1, $2, and $3 lines at the top.
publishStepDownload.description: Settings → Backup: a step of publishing a list. $1, $2, and $3 are the list’s header lines, shown as code: “! name:”, “! description:”, and “! author:”.

publishStepRepository.message: Create a public GitHub repository (or a gist) and add the file, e.g. $1.
publishStepRepository.description: Settings → Backup: a step of publishing a list. $1 is a file name, shown as code.

publishStepIssues.message: Add $1 so people can suggest sites to your list from the menu on each result.
publishStepIssues.description: Settings → Backup: a step of publishing a list. $1 is a header line, shown as code: “! issues: https://github.com/you/repo/issues”.

publishStepShare.message: Share the file’s link. People paste it into Lists → Add a list.
publishStepShare.description: Settings → Backup: a step of publishing a list. “Lists” is listsHeading, “Add a list” listsAddHeading.

publishStepDirectory.message: Want it under More lists for everyone? Open a pull request adding it to $1.
publishStepDirectory.description: Settings → Backup: a step of publishing a list. $1 is a link to a file, lists/directory.json. “More lists” is listsMoreHeading.

publishFormat.description: Settings → Backup: a link to the wiki page on the list format.

importIntro.message: Coming from uBlacklist or HOHSER? Paste your rules or export here and the sites join your list. Hidden stays hidden, HOHSER’s partial hide becomes Lower, and highlight colours become tags that highlight.
importIntro.description: Settings → Backup: under importHeading. uBlacklist and HOHSER are other extensions.

importHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

importPlaceholder.message: Paste uBlacklist rules, a HOHSER export, a Goggle, or one domain per line
importPlaceholder.description: Settings → Backup: placeholder of the field for sites to import.

importLabel.description: Settings → Backup: screen reader label of the field for sites to import.

importChooseFile.description: Settings → Backup: a button that fills the import field from a file.

importSourceHohser.description: For importRead: what the imported text was.

importSourceUblacklist.description: For importRead: what the imported text was.

importSourceGoggle.description: For importRead: what the imported text was. A Goggle is a Brave Search list.

importSourceAnubis.description: For importRead: what the imported text was.

importSourceDomains.description: For importRead: what the imported text was.

importRead_one.message: Read as $2: $1 site added and $3 updated.
importRead_one.description: After importing. $1 is how many sites were added, $2 what the text was (importSourceHohser…), $3 how many were updated.

importRead_other.message: Read as $2: $1 sites added and $3 updated.

importSkipped_one.message: $1 rule with address patterns or unsupported syntax left out; subscribe to the original list to keep them.
importSkipped_one.description: After importRead when some rules couldn’t be imported. $1 is how many.

importSkipped_other.message: $1 rules with address patterns or unsupported syntax left out; subscribe to the original list to keep them.

importFailed.description: After a failed import. $1 says what went wrong.

backupHeading.description: Settings → Backup: the sidebar’s name for the section, and the heading over the backup buttons.

backupIntro.message: Everything in one file: settings, tag choices, subscriptions, and your list.

backupRestoreFailed.description: After a backup failed to restore. $1 says what went wrong.

resetDone.message: Settings, tags, and subscriptions reset. Your list is kept.
resetDone.description: Settings → Backup: after Reset settings (resetButton), followed by an Undo button (summaryUndo).

settingsSections.description: Screen reader label of the settings sidebar.

settingsPageTitle.description: Tab title of the settings page. $1 is the open section, e.g. Tags.

settingsBrandTitle.description: Tooltip of Anubis’s name at the top of the settings sidebar.

settingsTagline.message: Hide, rank, and tag search results
settingsTagline.description: Under Anubis’s name at the top of the settings sidebar.

settingsSource.description: Link at the foot of the settings sidebar.

sitesHeading.description: Settings → Your sites: the section’s heading, also in the sidebar.

sitesHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

tagsHeading.description: Settings → Tags: the section’s heading, also in the sidebar.

tagsHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

listsHeading.description: Settings → Lists: the section’s heading, also in the sidebar.

listsHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

cleanupHeading.description: Settings → Remove panels: the section’s heading, also in the sidebar. Panels are the blocks on search pages that aren’t results: AI answers, videos, “People also ask”…

cleanupHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

appearanceHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

enginesHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

syncHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

shareHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

cleanupIntro.message: Anubis can remove the panels on search pages that aren’t results. Turn on each one you’d rather not see. “Show hidden” above the results brings them back for that search.
cleanupIntro.description: Settings → Remove panels: under the heading. “Show hidden” is showHidden.

cleanupEverySearch.description: Settings → Remove panels: heading over the switches, one for each kind of panel.

cleanupEverySearchHint.message: On means Anubis removes it. Off leaves it on the page.

cleanupStillShows.description: Link to the wiki’s troubleshooting page.

cleanupOnGoogle.description: Settings → Remove panels: heading over cleanupWebTab.

cleanupWebTab.description: Settings → Remove panels: a switch. Google’s “Web” tab shows only links.

cleanupWebTabHint.message: Sends every Google search to its Web tab: plain links, with no AI Overview, videos, or other panels, even ones Anubis doesn’t recognise. To leave it for one search, choose All above the results.
cleanupWebTabHint.description: Settings → Remove panels: explains cleanupWebTab. “AI Overview”, “Web”, and “All” are Google’s own names; use the ones Google shows in your language.

cleanupAi.description: Settings → Remove panels: a switch; on removes these panels from every search.

cleanupAiHint.message: Google’s AI Overview and AI Mode tab, DuckDuckGo’s AI-assisted answers and Duck.ai, Bing’s AI answers, and Brave’s AI answers.
cleanupAiHint.description: Settings → Remove panels: explains cleanupAi. AI Overview, AI Mode, and Duck.ai are the engines’ own names.

cleanupVideos.description: Settings → Remove panels: a switch; on removes these panels from every search.

cleanupVideosHint.message: Video and short-video panels between the results.

cleanupQuestions.description: Settings → Remove panels: a switch; on removes these panels from every search. Google’s own name for its list of questions; use the one Google shows in your language.

cleanupQuestionsHint.message: Lists of other people’s questions with expandable answers.

cleanupDiscussions.description: Settings → Remove panels: a switch; on removes these panels from every search.

cleanupDiscussionsHint.message: Panels of forum threads between the results, like Google’s “Discussions and forums”. Forum pages among the results stay.
cleanupDiscussionsHint.description: Settings → Remove panels: explains cleanupDiscussions. “Discussions and forums” is Google’s own name.

cleanupNews.description: Settings → Remove panels: a switch; on removes these panels from every search. Google’s own name for its news panel.

cleanupImages.description: Settings → Remove panels: a switch; on removes these panels from every search.

cleanupImagesHint.message: Rows of images between the results. The Images tab still works.

cleanupRelated.description: Settings → Remove panels: a switch; on removes these panels from every search.

cleanupRelatedHint.message: Lists of other searches, usually at the bottom of the page.

cleanupElsewhere.description: Settings → Remove panels: a switch; on removes these panels from every search.

cleanupElsewhereHint.message: Rows of buttons that repeat your search on another engine, like Brave’s “Find elsewhere”.
cleanupElsewhereHint.description: Settings → Remove panels: explains cleanupElsewhere. “Find elsewhere” is Brave’s own name.

sitesIntro.message: Sites you’ve ranked or hidden yourself. Your choice beats every list you subscribe to. Use the button on any search result, or add sites here.
sitesIntro.description: Settings → Your sites: under the heading.

sitesEditAsText.description: Settings → Your sites: a button that shows your list as text, and the heading over it.

sitesBackToTable.description: Settings → Your sites: the button sitesEditAsText becomes while the text is shown.

sitesTooBig.message: Your list is too big for browser sync, so it’s saved on this device only. Download it to keep a copy.

sitesAddPlaceholder.description: Settings → Your sites: placeholder of the field to add a site.

sitesAdd.description: Settings → Your sites: the button that adds the site typed in the field.

sitesNotDomain.message: That doesn’t look like a domain.
sitesNotDomain.description: Settings → Your sites: when the site typed in can’t be read.

sitesAddHint.message: It applies to the site and all its subdomains.
sitesAddHint.description: Settings → Your sites: under “Add a site” (popupAddSite).

sitesAddHelp.message: Choosing how much of a site
sitesAddHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

sitesFilter_one.description: Settings → Your sites: placeholder of the search field over the table. $1 is how many sites there are.

sitesFilterLabel.description: Settings → Your sites: screen reader label of the search field over the table.

sitesAddTagTo.description: Settings → Your sites: screen reader label of the menu that tags a site. $1 is a site.

sitesKeptNormal.message: Kept at normal, whatever your lists say
sitesKeptNormal.description: Settings → Your sites: under a site set to Normal on purpose.

sitesRemoveTag.description: Settings → Your sites: tooltip of a tag on a site. $1 is the tag’s name, $2 the site.

sitesForget.description: Settings → Your sites: tooltip and screen reader label of the × that drops a site from your list. $1 is the site.

sitesFirst500.message: Showing the first 500. Filter to find the rest.
sitesFirst500.description: Settings → Your sites: under the table when you have more than 500 sites.

sitesNone.message: No sites yet. Add one above, or use the button on a search result.
sitesNone.description: Settings → Your sites: in place of the table when your list is empty.

sitesTextLabel.description: Settings → Your sites: screen reader label of the text field.

sitesTextIntro.message: Your list in the Anubis list format: Brave Goggles syntax plus tags. It’s exactly the file you would publish. Lines the table can’t show are kept as written.
sitesTextIntro.description: Settings → Your sites: over the text field.

sitesTextReadable.description: Settings → Your sites: under the text field when every line can be read. $1 is listInstructions, $2 popupTagCount.

listInstructions_one.description: How many instructions (lines with a rule) a list has.

listErrorLine.description: A line of a list Anubis can’t read. $1 is the line number, $2 what’s wrong with it.

sitesSave.description: Settings → Your sites: saves the text.

sitesFormatReference.description: Settings → Your sites: a link to the wiki page on the list format.

listsIntro.message: Subscribe to lists that tag, rerank, or hide sites. Any text file on GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, or a gist works: Anubis lists, Brave Goggles, uBlacklist rulesets, and plain domain lists.

listsUpdateAll.description: Settings → Lists: a button that downloads every list again.

listsUpdating.description: Settings → Lists: listsUpdateAll while it works.

listsAddHeading.description: Settings → Lists: heading over the field for a list’s address.

listsAddHint.message: Paste a link to the file. Links to a GitHub page, a gist, or a Brave Goggle work too.

listsAddHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

listsUrlLabel.description: Settings → Lists: screen reader label of the field for a list’s address.

listsNone.message: No lists yet. Pick some from the ones below.
listsNone.description: Settings → Lists: under “Your lists” (welcomeListsHeading) when you subscribe to none.

listsMoreHeading.description: Settings → Lists: heading over lists you could subscribe to.

listsMoreIntro.message: From the Anubis directory and the wider community.

listsShare.message: Made a list worth sharing? Add it to the directory with a pull request to $1.
listsShare.description: Settings → Lists: at the foot of the page. $1 is a link to a file, lists/directory.json.

listsNeedHttps.message: Lists must be served over https.
listsNeedHttps.description: Settings → Lists: when a list’s address doesn’t start with https://.

listsPermissionToDownload.message: Anubis needs permission to read $1 to download this list.
listsPermissionToDownload.description: Settings → Lists: when the browser’s permission was refused. $1 is a website, e.g. example.org.

listsSubscribed.description: Settings → Lists: after subscribing. $1 is the list’s name, $2 listInstructions, $3 popupTagCount.

listsSubscribedBundled.message: Subscribed to $1 (using the copy bundled with Anubis until it can update).
listsSubscribedBundled.description: Settings → Lists: after subscribing when the download failed. $1 is the list’s name.

listsSubscribeFailed.description: Settings → Lists: after a failed subscription. $1 says what went wrong.

listsUse.description: Settings → Lists: screen reader label of a list’s on/off switch. $1 is the list’s name.

listsOn.description: Settings → Lists: tooltip of a list’s switch while the list is used.

listsOff.description: Settings → Lists: tooltip of a list’s switch while the list isn’t used.

listsUpdateFailed.description: Settings → Lists: after updating one list failed. $1 is the list’s name, $2 what went wrong.

listsUpToDate.description: Settings → Lists: after updating one list. $1 is the list’s name.

listsFacts.description: Settings → Lists: the facts under a list’s description, as a sentence. $1 is the facts joined: listInstructions, popupTagCount, listsBy, listsUpdated…

listsLinks.description: Settings → Lists: after listsFacts. $1 is the list’s links (listsHomepage, listsSuggestChanges), joined.

listsNotDownloaded.description: Settings → Lists: one of listsFacts, for a list with no copy yet.

listsBy.description: Settings → Lists: one of listsFacts. $1 is the list’s author.

listsBundledCopy.description: Settings → Lists: one of listsFacts, for a built-in list not downloaded yet.

listsUpdated.description: Settings → Lists: one of listsFacts. $1 is how long ago: timeJustNow, or “5 minutes ago” from the browser.

listsHomepage.description: Settings → Lists: a link after listsFacts.

listsSuggestChanges.description: Settings → Lists: a link after listsFacts, to the list’s issue tracker.

listsUsingBundled.message: Using the copy bundled with Anubis until it can update ($1).
listsUsingBundled.description: Settings → Lists: under a built-in list whose download failed. $1 says what went wrong.

listsLastUpdateFailed.description: Settings → Lists: under a list whose last download failed. $1 says what went wrong.

listsSkippedLines_one.message: $1 line skipped: Anubis can’t read that syntax yet.
listsSkippedLines_one.description: Settings → Lists: under a list with lines Anubis can’t read. $1 is how many.

listsSkippedLines_other.message: $1 lines skipped: Anubis can’t read that syntax yet.

listsUpdateNow.description: Settings → Lists: tooltip of a list’s update button.

listsUpdateOne.description: Settings → Lists: screen reader label of a list’s update button. $1 is the list’s name.

listsViewFile.description: Settings → Lists: tooltip of a link to a list’s file.

listsViewOne.description: Settings → Lists: screen reader label of the link to a list’s file. $1 is the list’s name.

listsUnsubscribe.description: Settings → Lists: tooltip of a list’s delete button.

listsUnsubscribeOne.description: Settings → Lists: screen reader label of a list’s delete button. $1 is the list’s name.

listLensTitle.message: A lens hides results the list doesn’t mention

listKindLens.description: What kind of list it is, after its format: a lens hides every result it doesn’t mention.

listKindBuiltin.description: What kind of list it is, after its format: it comes with Anubis.

listFormatGoggle.description: A list’s format. Goggles are Brave Search’s lists; keep the name.

listFormatUblacklist.description: A list’s format. uBlacklist is another extension; keep the name.

listFormatDomains.description: A list’s format: one domain per line.

timeNever.description: For a time that hasn’t happened, e.g. “updated never”.

timeJustNow.description: For a time less than a minute ago.

tagsIntro.message: Lists label results. You decide what each label does: follow the list, only show it, highlight it, or raise, lower, or hide what carries it. Lists that use the same tag name share it.

tagActionList.description: Settings → Tags: a choice of what a tag does: what the lists’ own rules say.

tagActionLabel.description: Settings → Tags: a choice of what a tag does: only show the tag.

tagActionHighlight.description: Settings → Tags: a choice of what a tag does: tint results in the tag’s colour.

tagActionFor.message: What to do with results tagged $1
tagActionFor.description: Settings → Tags: screen reader label of the menu of choices (tagActionList…). $1 is the tag’s name.

tagMarksNone.description: Settings → Tags: what a tag does, when no site has it.

tagMarks.description: Settings → Tags: starts the sentence saying what a tag does. $1 is tagMarksYours and tagMarksFromList, joined.

tagMarksYours_one.description: For tagMarks: how many sites in your own list carry the tag.

tagMarksFromList_one.description: For tagMarks: how many sites a list gives the tag. $2 is the list’s name.

tagEffectLabel.message: $1 Only a label: their ranking stays the same.
tagEffectLabel.description: Settings → Tags: what a tag does. $1 is tagMarks.

tagEffectHighlight.message: $1 Highlights them in the tag’s colour.
tagEffectHighlight.description: Settings → Tags: what a tag does. $1 is tagMarks.

tagEffectRaise.description: Settings → Tags: what a tag does. $1 is tagMarks.

tagEffectLower.description: Settings → Tags: what a tag does. $1 is tagMarks.

tagEffectHide.description: Settings → Tags: what a tag does. $1 is tagMarks.

tagEffectOneList.description: Settings → Tags: what a tag does when it follows one list: “Marks 60 sites from Official docs. Official docs raises 51 of them.” $1 is tagMarks, $2 the list’s name, $3 tagListRaises and the like, joined.

tagEffectLists.description: Settings → Tags: what a tag does when it follows several lists. $1 is tagMarks, $2 tagListsRaise and the like, joined.

tagListRaises_one.description: For tagEffectOneList: one list raises $1 of the sites.

tagListLowers_one.description: For tagEffectOneList: one list lowers $1 of the sites.

tagListHides_one.description: For tagEffectOneList: one list hides $1 of the sites.

tagListsRaise_one.description: For tagEffectLists: the lists raise $1 of the sites.

tagListsLower_one.description: For tagEffectLists: the lists lower $1 of the sites.

tagListsHide_one.description: For tagEffectLists: the lists hide $1 of the sites.

tagSitesToTag.description: Settings → Tags: screen reader label of the field that tags sites. $1 is the tag’s name.

tagAddSite.description: Settings → Tags: the button after tagSitesToTag’s field.

tagNotSite.description: Settings → Tags: when something typed isn’t a site. $1 is what was typed.

tagTypeSite.description: Settings → Tags: when the field is empty.

tagSiteNote.description: Saved in your list as the reason a site has a tag. $1 is the tag’s name, $2 the reason typed in.

tagMoreSites_one.description: Settings → Tags: after the first few sites a list gives a tag. $1 is how many more.

tagFromList.description: Settings → Tags: the sites a list gives a tag. $1 is the list’s name in bold, $2 its sites, joined.

tagName.description: Settings → Tags: screen reader label of a tag’s name field.

tagNameShort.description: Settings → Tags: label of a tag’s name field.

tagDescription.description: Settings → Tags: label of a tag’s description field.

tagDescriptionPlaceholder.description: Settings → Tags: placeholder of a tag’s description field.

tagMeaning.description: Settings → Tags: screen reader label of a tag’s description field. $1 is the tag’s name.

tagYourSites.description: Settings → Tags: heading in an open tag.

tagNoSites.message: None yet. Add one here, or use the ⚖ button on a search result.
tagNoSites.description: Settings → Tags: under tagYourSites when you’ve tagged no site.

tagFromYourLists.description: Settings → Tags: heading over the sites lists give a tag.

tagColour.description: Settings → Tags: tooltip of a tag’s colour picker.

tagColourOf.description: Settings → Tags: screen reader label of a tag’s colour picker. $1 is the tag’s name.

tagShowUnder.description: Settings → Tags: screen reader label of a tag’s switch. $1 is the tag’s name.

tagShowTitle.description: Settings → Tags: tooltip of a tag’s switch.

tagEdit.description: Settings → Tags: opens a tag’s name, description, and sites.

tagDone.description: Settings → Tags: tagEdit while the tag is open: closes it.

tagEditLabel.description: Settings → Tags: screen reader label of tagEdit. $1 is the tag’s name.

tagDelete.description: Settings → Tags: tooltip and screen reader label of the button that deletes one of your tags. $1 is the tag’s name.

tagNewHeading.description: Settings → Tags: heading over the form that creates a tag.

tagNewHint.message: Your tags are saved in your list, so they go with it when you publish it.

tagNewHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

tagNewPlaceholder.description: Settings → Tags: placeholder of the new tag’s name.

tagNewColour.description: Settings → Tags: screen reader label of the new tag’s colour picker.

tagCreate.description: Settings → Tags: the button that creates the tag.

tagNameInvalid.message: Give the tag a name with at least one letter or number.
tagNameInvalid.description: Settings → Tags: when the new tag’s name can’t be used.

tagExists.message: There is already a tag called “$1”.
tagExists.description: Settings → Tags: when a tag with that name exists. $1 is its name.

tagAllHeading.description: Settings → Tags: heading over every tag.

tagNone.message: No tags yet. Subscribe to a list or create one above.
tagNone.description: Settings → Tags: when there are no tags.

quoted.description: A name in quotation marks, such as a tag’s. Use your language’s quotation marks.

reasonPins.description: In the menu on a result, under Why: what a list does to the result, after the list’s name. Parts are joined: “raises it by 3 and tags it “Docs””.

reasonKeepsNormal.description: In the menu on a result, under Why: what a list does to the result, after the list’s name.

reasonHides.description: In the menu on a result, under Why: what a list does to the result, after the list’s name.

reasonRaises.description: In the menu on a result, under Why: what a list does to the result, after the list’s name. $1 is a number of places.

reasonLowers.description: In the menu on a result, under Why: what a list does to the result, after the list’s name. $1 is a number of places.

reasonTags.description: In the menu on a result, under Why: what a list does to the result, after the list’s name. $1 is one or more tag names, each in quoted, joined.

reasonMentions.description: In the menu on a result, under Why: what a list does to the result, after the list’s name. For a rule that only names the site.

reasonLens.message: doesn’t include it, so it’s hidden
reasonLens.description: In the menu on a result, under Why: what a list does to the result, after the list’s name. For a lens, a list that hides everything it doesn’t name.

reasonYourTagSettings.description: In the menu on a result, under Why: stands for a list’s name when your own tag choices moved or hid the result.

reasonLine.description: Tooltip of the ranking label under a result, one line per list. $1 is the list’s name, $2 what it does (reasonRaises…).

menuReason.description: In the menu on a result, under Why: one list’s reason as a sentence. $1 is the list’s name in bold, $2 what it does (reasonRaises…).

choiceHide.description: After reasonYourTagSettings: your tag choices hide the result. $1 is the tags, each in quoted, joined.

choiceRaise_one.description: After reasonYourTagSettings: your choice for a tag raises the result. $1 is how many tags, $2 the places, $3 the tags, each in quoted, joined.

choiceLower_one.description: Like choiceRaise, for tags you lower.

choiceTotal.description: After reasonYourTagSettings, when tags both raise and lower: $1 is choiceRaise and choiceLower joined, $2 choiceNetUp, choiceNetDown, or choiceNetSame.

choiceNetUp_one.description: For choiceTotal. $1 is a number of places.

choiceNetDown_one.description: For choiceTotal. $1 is a number of places.

choiceNetSame.message: so it stays where it was

lineBadTagDefinition.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is the line’s text after “! tag:”.

lineNeedsPattern.message: Instruction needs a pattern or a site
lineNeedsPattern.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine).

lineTooLong.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is a number.

lineBadSite.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is what the line gives as a site.

lineBadStrength.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is an option of the list format, boost or downrank (keep it as it is), $2 the largest number allowed.

lineBadTagId.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is what the line gives as a tag.

lineUnknownOption.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is the option, a word of the list format.

lineEmptyPattern.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine).

lineTooManyWildcards.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is a number.

lineTooManySeparators.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is a number.

lineIfGuard.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). @if is part of the uBlacklist format; keep it as it is.

lineRegexTooLong.message: Regular expression is longer than $1 characters
lineRegexTooLong.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is a number.

lineRegexFreeze.message: Regular expression could freeze search pages (a repeated group repeats inside): $1
lineRegexFreeze.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is the line.

lineBadRegex.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is the line.

lineUnsupported.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is the line.

lineBadHost.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is the host the line gives.

lineMatchesEverything.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine).

lineNotDomain.description: Why a line of a list can’t be read, after “Line 12:” (listErrorLine). $1 is the line.

listTooBig.description: Why a list couldn’t be downloaded. $1 is a number of megabytes.

listIsWebPage.message: Got a web page, not a list. Use the raw file URL.
listIsWebPage.description: Why a list couldn’t be downloaded.

listTimedOut.description: Why a list couldn’t be downloaded: it took too long.

listNoUsableRules.description: Why a list couldn’t be used. $1 is a line number, $2 what’s wrong with it (lineBadSite…).

listNoRules.description: Why a list couldn’t be used.

backupNotBackup.description: Why a file couldn’t be restored.

themeAuto.description: A colour scheme: follow the browser’s light or dark mode.

themeAutoTitle.description: Tooltip and screen reader label of themeAuto, which may show as an icon only.

themeLightTitle.description: Tooltip and screen reader label of themeLight, which may show as an icon only.

themeDarkTitle.description: Tooltip and screen reader label of themeDark, which may show as an icon only.

personalListName.description: The name your own list goes by, wherever Anubis shows a list’s name: “Your list hides it”.

importHighlightTag.description: The name of a tag made when importing from HOHSER, whose highlight colours are numbered. $1 is the number.

tagDeleted_one.message: Deleted the tag “$2” and removed it from $1 site.
tagDeleted_one.description: Settings → Tags: after deleting one of your tags, followed by an Undo button (summaryUndo). $1 is how many of your sites had it, $2 the tag’s name.

tagDeleted_other.message: Deleted the tag “$2” and removed it from $1 sites.

listsUnsubscribed.description: Settings → Lists: after unsubscribing, followed by an Undo button (summaryUndo). $1 is the list’s name.
